stem:
Krish is told that carbon dioxide forms when carbon and oxygen join chemically. The gas's properties differ from those of carbon and oxygen. He cannot get carbon back from the gas by sieving or filtering.

Which claims correctly classify carbon dioxide? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Carbon dioxide is a compound because carbon and oxygen are chemically joined.
Carbon dioxide is a compound because its properties differ from those of carbon and oxygen.
Carbon dioxide is a mixture because it is made from more than one element.
Carbon dioxide is a compound only because the gas looks colourless.

teacher.key_rationale: A compound has different elements chemically joined and properties unlike those elements. Calling it a mixture swaps the term; judging only from colour is a surface feature.
